messages:
jess: Heads-up — I'm planning a compatibility sweep and fallback policy sanity check for the runtime unpin from v3.2.0 -> v3.3.0. Target window: 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC (canary first, then staggered). Need confirmation on models we should keep soft-pinned (KV-cache / longseq risk) and the rollback triggers we want in the deploybot runbook.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary: runtime v3.3.0 on pool:canary-gpu at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. Canary size: 10 nodes. Auto-fallback: enabled. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-unpin-sanity 

mike: +1 on canary. Quick Q: do we need an SDK pin for the client lib? I remember an edge where v2 SDK doesn't handle new kvcache headers.

anya: For quantized LLAMA3 variants, keep soft-pin in EU for 48h. We saw perf variance last time. Suggest explicit telemetry checks for generation latency and top-k divergence.

leo: Regional rollout note — EU region should have expanded fallback routing to dedicated-capacity if hosted capacity saturates. Suggest routing policy: prefer region-local model variant -> fallback to compatible quantized variant -> finally route to dedicated fallback (same model family).

sre-oncall: Rollback triggers proposal: 
- error rate spike > 2% sustained for 5m on canary
- p95 generation latency increase > 200ms vs baseline for 5m
- sampling quality regression (BLEU/embedding drift) > threshold on alert eval set
If any trigger fires, deploybot should auto-reroute new requests to previous runtime and alert #incidents.

carlos: Can someone paste the telemetry query we'll use in the runbook? I can add it to the oncall dashboard.

jess: Sure. Minimal p95 check we will run: 
```
from metrics
| where service=="runtime" and runtime_version=="v3.3.0" and env=="canary"
| summarize p95_latency = percentile(latency_ms, 95) by bin(1m, timestamp)
| where p95_latency > baseline_p95 + 200
```
Replace `baseline_p95` with the last 24h rolling median of canary-compatible nodes.

mike: SDK action: I'll open a tiny patch to add runtime header parsing compatibility and ship a 2.1.3 client tomorrow morning — but we'll gate it behind feature flag. If anything breaks, clients will still talk to old runtime.

anya: For model list: please soft-pin these for 48h in EU: `llama3-q8a-eu`, `redwood-gptx-quant-v2`, `longseq-guard-1`. Others can be unpinned.

deploy-bot: Noted config updates: added `soft_pin: 48h` for `llama3-q8a-eu`, `redwood-gptx-quant-v2`, `longseq-guard-1` in region EU. Fallback routing rule appended: `route_priority: [local_variant, quant_fallback, dedicated_fallback]`

leo: Thanks — small tweak: make dedicated_fallback only for premium customers; regular tier should go to cross-region hosted fallback instead.

jess: Agreed. Update runbook: add tier-aware fallback table and add explicit rollback step to re-pin runtime in deploybot if auto-reroute fails.

carlos: Done — adding the telemetry query and rollback triggers to the dashboard. Will add runbook snippet to oncall mobile alerts too.

sre-oncall: I'll be on-call during the window. If deploybot fires an auto-revert, please @sre-oncall immediately.

mike: +1. I'll post a short release note for product about the soft-pin exceptions and expected risk.

jess: Perfect. Plan stands: canary 02:00 UTC -> 3-hour observation -> staggered rollouts with region & tier-aware fallback. If no problems, lift EU soft-pins after 48h. I'll kick the deploybot tomorrow at 01:30 to warm nodes. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: warmup nodes for canary at 2026-03-22T01:30:00Z.

leo: ACK

anya: ACK

carlos: ACK

mike: ACK

jess: Thanks everyone — will reopen thread if any change.
